title: The Case of the Furisode at the Hidden Hot Spring on a Snowy Night
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. case_type: murder. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep379-380...) actually named the correct culprit (Eri Akechi) and roughly the correct kill order (Asuka before Ema), so no culprit-flip correction was needed here -- unlike some other rebuilds. What it got wrong/omitted: (1) it never captured that 'Eri Akechi' is a public misreading of the culprit's real name, Chieri Ake, and that she is the older sister of Sakurako Suzuka, the university student whose suicide five years earlier is the entire motive -- without that identity reveal the case has no solvable motive layer; (2) its single event e2 conflates two distinct physical tricks into one action ('freezes obi sashes to slide the weapon and a prop doll down a slope to the pond' as part of stabbing Asuka) when the transcript actually separates them: wooden planks were used to fake shallow footprints while Eri walked to/from the shrine to kill Ema, and separately, ice-frozen obi sashes (which melt back into ordinary cloth on contact with hot spring water) were used afterward to slide the murder knife and Ema's blood-stained bandana down the cliff from Eri's room into the women's hot spring, faking the kill order and building her own alibi; (3) it omitted the forged letter that framed producer Kyoichi Bando, the dry-ice-timed prop doll that faked the Furisode-Hannya curse at the moment of discovery, the red-herring accusation against Harumi Fukatsu (grief-driven suspicion, formally raised but false), and the tribute dolls Eri left at the shrine before the murders as a foreshadowing detail; (4) it had zero named characters beyond the four suspects and two victims -- Sakurako Suzuka (the actual reason for everything) wasn't a node at all.
